name: Discharge emergency patients home with instructions and follow-up
summary: When the emergency physician decides a patient can go home, the physician explains the diagnosis, writes prescriptions and, for about one patient in six, a referral to the fracture clinic or another hospital clinic. A nurse removes lines, takes final vital signs and goes over written instructions, the clerk closes the visit and the stretcher is cleaned for the next patient. Afterwards the physician's ED record is typed or dictated and transcribed, signed, and sent to the family physician through the provincial Health Report Manager or by fax, and the paper parts of the chart are scanned and released to coding. The patient part is short, but nurses are pulled to sicker patients, so discharged patients wait for line removal and teaching, and the record reaches the family physician a day or more later.

baseline.org_archetype: A not-for-profit Ontario community hospital corporation with three hospitals, about 640 inpatient beds and an emergency department at each site, on a single hospital information system with an electronic bed board.
baseline.notes: Ontario patients receive paper prescriptions and printed instructions in this period; physician documentation is a mix of typed notes in the hospital information system and dictation.

unit_of_work: one ED discharge (discharge decision to the ED record reaching the family physician and the chart released to coding)
trigger: The ED physician (or a consultant) decides after assessment that the patient can go home.
end_state: The patient has left with instructions, prescriptions and any clinic appointment; the ED record has been sent to the family physician where there is one; and the chart is complete and released to health records for coding.

volume.seasonality: Higher in winter (respiratory illness) and in summer (injuries); 2020/21 was about 20% lower during the first COVID-19 waves.

evidence.note: ED visits of 10,530 to 13,420 a month (organisation file) times the discharged-home share of NACRS visits, 78.8% to 79.9% in 2018/19 to 2021/22 (cihi_nacrs). The organisation file's 8,800 to 11,400 (mode 10,900, about 84%) leaves too little room for admissions (11%), patients who leave without being seen (4.5% to 6.9%) and transfers (about 2.5%).

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Winter respiratory season raises ED visits by a few percent; most of the extra patients are discharged home. Same parameters as the organisation file.
About 15 to 20 minutes per discharge for the explanation, prescriptions, referrals and the ED record. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.
Line removal, final vital signs and teaching for patients in the acute and intermediate areas (about 55%). Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.
Fast-track and minor-treatment discharges (about 45%). Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.
Referral faxes and bookings, rides, closing the visit. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.
Cleaning and restocking the stretcher or chair after each discharge. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.
Typing dictated ED notes (about a third of visits). Not listed among the process roles in the organisation file. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.

roles.title: Health records clerk (release of information, scanning)

evidence.note: Faxing ED records to family physicians not on HRM, scanning paper chart parts and releasing charts to coding. Not listed among the process roles in the organisation file. Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35) are taken from the organisation file.

systems.name: Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)
Fax (referrals, requisitions and reports to community physicians)
Home and community care referral portal (Health Partner Gateway)
Document imaging and scanning of paper chart forms
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones
Health Report Manager (OntarioMD) delivery of hospital reports to community EMRs

resources.name: Emergency treatment spaces, large site (stretchers, chairs and resuscitation bays)

steps.name: Explain diagnosis and write prescriptions
steps.description: The ED physician returns to the patient with the test results, explains the diagnosis and the plan, writes paper prescriptions and enters the discharge disposition and diagnosis in the hospital information system, choosing a standard instruction sheet for the condition (for example head injury, abdominal pain or a cast).

error.defect_description: Prescription dose or interaction error, or wrong instruction sheet.

control.basis: Discharge decision and prescriptions by a physician or nurse practitioner (Medicine Act and hospital medical staff rules).

evidence.note: Author's estimate. The 17% referral share covers fracture clinic, specialty clinic and next-day ED recheck appointments.

steps.name: Complete a clinic referral
steps.description: For fractures, sprains, eye problems or abnormal results needing specialist review, the physician fills in the fracture clinic or specialty clinic referral form (paper or electronic) with the reason and urgency, and attaches the X-ray report or results.

error.defect_description: Referral missing urgency or contact details, so the clinic cannot book it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Fax or book the referral
steps.description: The ED unit clerk books the fracture clinic slot directly in the clinic schedule or faxes the referral to the specialty clinic or community specialist, and writes the appointment or 'clinic will call you' on the patient's instructions.

error.defect_description: Fax not received or misfiled, so the patient is never called.

evidence.note: Author's estimate. Fax was the main referral channel in Ontario in this period.

steps.name: Remove lines and take final vital signs
steps.description: The ED nurse removes the IV and any monitoring, takes and records final vital signs and checks that ordered medications and pain control are done and the patient is safe to walk or be taken out. Discharged patients wait here when the nurse is caring for sicker patients.

error.defect_description: Vital signs abnormal but not escalated before discharge.

evidence.note: Author's estimate. The wait reflects nurses being pulled to new or unstable patients.

steps.name: Teach discharge instructions
steps.description: The ED nurse goes over the printed instruction sheet and prescriptions with the patient and family, asks them to repeat the warning signs and when to return, and checks they have a way home. The patient signs that instructions were received.

error.defect_description: Patient leaves without understanding the return warnings.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Finish fast-track treatment
steps.description: In the fast-track or minor-treatment area the RPN applies the dressing, splint or tensor bandage ordered, gives the last dose of medication and records final vital signs.

error.defect_description: Splint applied too tight or wrong position.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Teach fast-track discharge instructions
steps.description: The RPN reviews the condition-specific instruction sheet, wound or cast care and prescriptions with the patient, explains when to return and gives the clinic appointment if one was booked.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Refer a frail patient to home care
steps.description: For an older patient who can go home only with support, the ED nurse completes a home and community care referral in the Health Partner Gateway (or by fax) for nursing, personal support or a care coordinator visit, and confirms with the family.

error.defect_description: Referral incomplete; home care visit is delayed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate. Hospitals refer to home and community care through the Health Partner Gateway.

steps.name: Arrange a ride home
steps.description: When the patient has no ride (often at night or for older patients), the unit clerk phones family or arranges a taxi voucher, and the patient waits in a chair so the stretcher can be used.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the visit in ADT and the tracking board
steps.description: The ED unit clerk records the departure time, discharges the patient in ADT and removes them from the tracking board, which sets the ED length of stay reported to NACRS and starts the stretcher clean.

error.defect_description: Departure time entered late or not at all, overstating the ED stay.

control.basis: Mandatory NACRS reporting of ED visit time stamps to CIHI and the provincial wait time information system.

evidence.note: ED length of stay runs from registration to the time the patient leaves the ED. Times tier C.

steps.name: Clean and restock the stretcher or chair
steps.description: The ED patient care assistant strips the stretcher, wipes it and the equipment with disinfectant wipes, restocks supplies and marks the space ready on the tracking board.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the ED physician record
steps.description: The physician completes the ED record: history, findings, results, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up plan, either typed into the hospital information system template or dictated by phone for transcription. Most physicians finish charts between patients or at the end of the shift.

error.defect_description: Diagnosis or follow-up plan missing from the note.

control.basis: Public Hospitals Act Regulation 965 record-keeping and CPSO medical records expectations.

next.condition: typed or templated in the HIS

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the split between dictation and typed notes varies by hospital and physician.

steps.name: Transcribe the dictated note
steps.description: A medical transcriptionist types the dictated ED note into the hospital information system from the dictation queue, checking drug names and spelling, and sends it to the physician's inbox for signature.

error.defect_description: Transcription error in a drug name or dose.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a 12 to 48 hour transcription backlog.

steps.name: Review and sign the transcribed note
steps.description: The physician opens the draft in the inbox, corrects errors and electronically signs it. Signatures are often batched at the start of the next shift, which may be days later.

control.basis: Physician authentication of the medical record (hospital medical staff rules on chart completion).

evidence.note: Author's estimate. ED physicians work irregular shifts, so the delay to signature is long and variable.

steps.name: Send the ED record through Health Report Manager
steps.description: When the note is final, the hospital information system sends the ED report to the family physician named on the visit through Health Report Manager, which delivers it into the physician's EMR; an ED discharge eNotification may already have been sent at departure.

error.defect_description: Wrong or outdated family physician on the registration record, so the report goes to the wrong office.

evidence.note: HRM delivers hospital ED reports to clinicians named on the report and more than 200 hospital sites are connected; eNotifications on ED discharge. The HRM coverage share is tier C.

steps.name: Fax the ED record to the family physician
steps.description: For family physicians not on HRM, a health records clerk prints or queues the signed ED record and faxes it to the clinic's fax number, checking the number against the physician directory.

error.defect_description: Faxed to the wrong number, a privacy breach.

control.basis: Personal Health Information Protection Act safeguards for disclosure by fax.

evidence.note: HRM FAQ notes that some facilities keep sending fax or paper alongside HRM. Times tier C.

steps.name: Scan the paper chart and release it to coding
steps.description: A health records clerk collects the ED paper forms (triage sheet, nursing notes, signed instructions, consent), scans and indexes them to the visit in the document imaging system, checks the physician note is signed and releases the chart to the coding work queue.

error.defect_description: Page scanned to the wrong patient or visit.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: daily scanning batches.

steps.name: Check chart completeness
steps.description: The clerk runs the incomplete-chart list for ED visits and returns charts with missing physician signatures or diagnoses to the physician's deficiency queue; complete charts go to coding for NACRS abstracting.

control.basis: NACRS abstracting requires a complete ED record; deficiency tracking under hospital health records policy.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Clinic referral
exceptions.description: The physician refers the patient to the fracture clinic or another clinic and the clerk books or faxes the referral.

exceptions.name: Home care referral
exceptions.description: A frail patient goes home only with home care services arranged.

exceptions.name: Ride needed
exceptions.description: The patient waits in a chair while family or a taxi is arranged.

exceptions.name: Dictated note
exceptions.description: The ED note is dictated, transcribed and signed before it can be sent, adding one to several days.

exceptions.name: Fax to family physician
exceptions.description: The family physician is not on HRM and the record is faxed.

exceptions.name: Incomplete chart returned
exceptions.description: The chart is returned to the physician for a missing signature or diagnosis.

benchmarks.unit: days from discharge decision to chart released to coding

evidence.note: Author's estimate: patient part under an hour; typed notes completed within the shift; paper chart parts scanned in next-business-day batches (longer over weekends); dictated notes add 1 to 5 days for transcription and signature.

benchmarks.unit: minutes from registration to leaving the ED
benchmarks.population: Patients discharged home, all NACRS-reporting EDs in Canada

evidence.note: Table 2; the discharge process is the last 20 to 60 minutes of this stay.
Author's estimate; no Ontario source found that reports this interval separately.
Targets stated by Ontario Health.

pain_points.description: Patients who are ready to go wait for a nurse to remove the IV and teach, because nurses are pulled to new and unstable patients; the stretcher stays occupied meanwhile.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: Dictated notes wait for transcription and then for the physician to sign, so the family physician gets the record days later and the patient may be seen before it arrives.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Referrals and ED records sent by fax go missing or to the wrong number; patients are not called for clinic follow-up.

evidence.note: Fax remained in use alongside HRM; the error rates are tier C.

pain_points.description: Patients who leave without understanding warning signs or without follow-up return to the ED, some needing admission within 72 hours, which hospitals must audit.

evidence.note: Ontario ED Return Visit Quality Program audits 72-hour and 7-day returns that lead to admission.

sources.title: NACRS Emergency Department Visits: Volumes and Median Lengths of Stay, 2003-2004 to 2021-2022, Supplementary Statistics (data tables)
sources.supports: Table 2, all reporting EDs: median ED length of stay for admitted patients 702, 720, 642 and 786 minutes and for patients discharged home 174, 180, 168 and 192 minutes in 2018/19 to 2021/22; admitted share of visits 10.6%, 10.6%, 12.4% and 11.2%; discharged home share 79.4%, 78.8%, 79.9% and 78.9%; left without being seen 4.5% to 6.9%.

sources.title: Time Spent in Emergency Departments
sources.supports: Provincial ED length-of-stay targets: 8 hours for admitted patients and high-urgency discharged patients, 4 hours for low-urgency discharged patients; admitted length of stay includes the wait for an inpatient bed.

sources.title: Health Report Manager: frequently asked questions
sources.supports: HRM delivers hospital medical record reports (such as ED reports and discharge summaries) to the clinicians named on the report, in their EMR; provincial expansion began in 2013 and more than 200 hospital sites are connected; some facilities keep sending paper or fax alongside HRM; eNotifications on ED discharge.

sources.title: Health Report Manager eNotifications
sources.supports: Near real-time HRM message to the primary care provider when a patient is discharged from the ED; discharge summaries and other reports follow once the hospital has prepared them; guideline of follow-up within 7 days of discharge.

sources.title: Value-for-Money Audit: Emergency Departments (2023 Annual Report)
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Average wait for an inpatient bed after the decision to admit: about 8 to 10 hours before COVID-19, 13 hours (90th percentile 35 hours) in 2022/23, about 21 hours at the 90th percentile in 2013/14; Mississauga Halton sub-region average 10.8 hours in 2021/22 and 21.3 hours in 2022/23; 12% of ED visits admitted in 2022/23; ALC about 15% of patient days; at least 1,000 hallway patients a day in January 2019; ED Return Visit Quality Program (72-hour and 7-day returns).

assumptions: The process starts when the physician decides to discharge; registration, triage, assessment and tests belong to earlier ED processes.
Volume follows the CIHI discharged-home share (about 79%) applied to the organisation file's ED visits, which is lower than the organisation file's process map entry.
ED space occupancy (s04, s06, s11) is split across the three sites by expected share (55%, 30%, 15%), so each figure is the expected minutes per case, not one patient's minutes.

The split between dictated (35%) and typed (65%) notes, the HRM coverage of family physicians (about 68% of patients with a family physician) and the 15% of patients without one are author's estimates.

Transcription and chart scanning are done by the transcriptionist and health records clerk roles from the organisation file; the process map entry lists neither. Transcription itself is the dh-transcription process; s13 is its share of the work.
Physician cost uses the organisation file's estimated clinical earnings; physicians are paid by OHIP, not the hospital.
